title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Severity of a Missed Response and the Credit Rate
content:
Where the call the credit arises from was accepted at emergency or critical priority and the technician
reached the building on a later calendar day than the day the call was accepted, the tier's credit rate
is taken at 1.5. Where the call was accepted at routine or priority and the technician reached the
building on a later calendar day than the day the call was accepted, the tier's credit rate is taken at
0.5. In any other case neither multiple nor share is taken of the tier's credit rate.

The priority is the classification the call was accepted at, as the dispatch record carries it; the
later calendar day is judged between the day the call was accepted and the day the technician reached
the building, as the call's own records carry them.

**The credit rate each program of the Demand Service Rate Programs publishes**, on which the multiple or the share is taken:

| Program | Credit rate (percent of the labor charge) |
|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 0 |
| Priority Response Program | 25 |
| Block Hour Service Program | 25 |
| Emergency Response Program | 50 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 100 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 100 |

| The priority the call was accepted at | The day the technician reached the building | The credit rate |
|---|---|---|
| emergency or critical | a later calendar day than the day of acceptance | the tier's credit rate taken at 1.5 |
| routine or priority | a later calendar day than the day of acceptance | the tier's credit rate taken at 0.5 |
| any | the same calendar day as the day of acceptance | neither multiple nor share is taken |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** On the Emergency Response Program, whose credit rate is 50 percent, a
call accepted at emergency priority whose technician arrived the following calendar day carries a rate
of 75 percent; had the same call been accepted at routine priority, the rate would be 25 percent. On the
Time & Material Account, whose credit rate is 0, a multiple or share of that rate is still 0.
